tasks.locator: Discussion › Limitations and Strengths, 1st paragraph; Conclusions, 1st paragraph; Abstract › Conclusions and Relevance
tasks.extracted: Limitations stated by the authors: AUDADIS interviewers were not clinicians, though a NESARC-III validation substudy comparing AUDADIS and clinician diagnoses of 12-month AUD is said to have shown similar prevalence and good concordance; neither survey covered homeless or incarcerated people; the NESARC-III response rate (60.1%) was lower than NESARC's (81.0%). The authors state that weighting that compensated for non-response made the surveys comparable and that agreement with other studies showing increases in alcohol-related indicators over the same period supports the validity of the increases. The abstract and the Conclusions present the increases in alcohol use, high-risk drinking and DSM-IV AUD as real and call them a public health crisis; this paper does not mention the stable NSDUH AUD figure reported in Grant et al. (2015).
